inspection_summary: Inspected all 878 logical normalized lines. The frozen line count is recovered by treating the embedded FS/GS extraction separators as line boundaries, while the SHA-256 matches exactly. The article converts moment bounds into upper-tail estimates, bounds log|zeta| by a short prime sum using the favorable sign of the zero contribution under RH, controls the resulting Dirichlet polynomials by high moments, and sketches symmetry-sensitive transfers to three L-function families.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic identity, title, and dedication only.

sections_inspected.label: Abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the RH-conditional near-conjectural moment upper bound and extension to L-function families.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Sets the moment problem, reduces moments to large-value frequencies, states the three-regime tail theorem and prime-sum proposition, and derives the moment and concentration corollaries.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Proof of the main proposition
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses Hadamard factorization, an integrated logarithmic-derivative identity, and a parameter choice that makes the zero term nonpositive.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Proof of the theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Removes prime powers, proves a high-moment mean-value estimate, splits the prime polynomial by scale, and optimizes tail bounds in the required regimes.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Moments of L-functions in families
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transfers the method to unitary, symplectic, and orthogonal families and isolates the prime-square contribution that shifts the Gaussian center.

accepted_units.title: One-sided prime-sum majorant for log|zeta|
accepted_units.why_material: States the central move: for an upper bound, nearby zeros are benign and log|zeta| can be majorized by a weighted short von Mangoldt sum plus an explicit length penalty.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1. The sign mechanism is only asserted here; lines 270-424 are needed to expose why the zero term can be discarded.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact coefficients and admissible parameter range depend on an OCR-risky display; the prose safely supports the one-sided prime-sum mechanism.

accepted_units.title: Tail bounds yield moments and locate the dominant value band
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how crude forms of the tail theorem inserted into the layer-cake identity give the upper moment bound and how removing unusually small or large values leaves the dominant moment contribution.
accepted_units.context_note: Uses the large-value set and moment identity defined earlier; no additional source context is needed beyond that linked unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact exponents are displayed-formula dependent; the prose clearly states the two tail regimes and concentration conclusion.

accepted_units.title: Integrating the logarithmic derivative turns zeros into a nonnegative control term
accepted_units.why_material: Defines a nonnegative zero sum under RH, derives it from Hadamard factorization, and integrates in the real direction to compare the critical-line value with an off-line value plus a signed zero contribution.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the first half of the main proposition proof and supplies the semantic reason nearby zeros help a one-sided upper bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The identities (4) and (5) and the definition of F(s) are formula-image sensitive, though their sign and integration roles are explicit in checked prose.

accepted_units.title: Selberg-type smoothed explicit formula from contour shifting
accepted_units.why_material: Derives a finite von Mangoldt sum plus zero, pole, and trivial-zero terms by integrating a logarithmic derivative kernel and shifting the contour, furnishing the algebraic bridge to primes.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof is self-contained at the mechanism level and feeds directly into the integrated estimate that follows.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Residue terms and kernel powers are OCR-sensitive; contour-shift and term-matching logic are recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: Choose the horizontal shift so the zero contribution cancels
accepted_units.why_material: Integrates the explicit formula, bounds its zero contribution by F(s0), combines it with the earlier critical-line comparison, and chooses the shift parameter so the remaining F(s0) coefficient is nonpositive.
accepted_units.context_note: Completes the proof-level explanation missing from the carried prime-sum proposition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The cancellation threshold and coefficients rely on equations (6) and (7); the checked final prose explicitly states the negative-contribution criterion.

accepted_units.title: Reduce the von Mangoldt polynomial to primes
accepted_units.why_material: Separates higher prime powers, controls prime squares via an RH explicit-formula estimate and partial summation, and shows their total cost is only logarithmic at the third iterated scale.
accepted_units.context_note: Provides the approximation needed before probabilistic high-moment control can be applied to a prime polynomial.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prime-square bound is display-dependent and OCR-risky; the decomposition and partial-summation route are explicit.

accepted_units.title: High moments are controlled by diagonal combinatorics
accepted_units.why_material: Expands a prime Dirichlet polynomial to the kth power, separates diagonal from off-diagonal terms, uses the length constraint to absorb the latter, and bounds the diagonal by k! times the coefficient variance.
accepted_units.context_note: This lemma is the reusable concentration engine for both short and long prime blocks.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Multinomial coefficients and off-diagonal estimates are formula-heavy; the expansion, diagonal split, and length condition are readable in prose.

accepted_units.title: Split the prime polynomial into short and long scales
accepted_units.why_material: Carries the v1 scale-decomposition unit linking the proposition and mean-value lemma to two alternative large-deviation events for a point in S(T,V).
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1. Its inherited span begins in the preceding lemma and stops before the two events are fully optimized, so lines 428-660 are the required bounded repair context.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The piecewise parameter A and definitions of S1 and S2 depend on extraction-risky displays; the prose establishes the scale split and either-or event.

accepted_units.title: Optimize high moments separately for the long and short prime blocks
accepted_units.why_material: Chooses scale parameters, converts membership in the large-value set into one of two prime-block deviations, applies the mean-value lemma with different moment choices, and combines their bounds to prove the theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: Overlaps the carried decomposition where necessary and supplies its missing endpoint through both optimized estimates.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The piecewise A, moment choices, and estimates (8)-(9) are formula-layer dependent; prose securely supports the two-block optimization mechanism.

accepted_units.title: Unitary-family transfer replaces time averaging by character orthogonality
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies the sole structural modification for primitive characters: character orthogonality controls the analogue of the off-diagonal terms in the mean-value lemma.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a sketch rather than a full derivation and remains GRH-conditional.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The moment exponents are displayed-formula dependent; the replacement of the averaging mechanism is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Prime squares shift the center for quadratic Dirichlet L-values
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that prime squares are no longer negligible, contribute half a log-log term, and force a shifted large-value threshold before reciprocity and Polya-Vinogradov provide the mean-value analogue.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof is intentionally sketched; the stated tail and moment bounds are conditional on GRH and the named family-specific averaging tools.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact shifts and exponents are formula-sensitive; the prime-square cause and shifted threshold are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Prime squares shift the center oppositely for elliptic-curve twists
accepted_units.why_material: Repeats the explicit-formula architecture with elliptic-curve coefficients and finds a negative half-log-log prime-square contribution, producing the orthogonal-family moment exponent.
accepted_units.context_note: A method sketch only; it records the structural difference rather than a complete family proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Euler-factor coefficients, signs, and threshold formulas need scan verification; the prose recovers the prime-square shift and resulting tail route.

accepted_units.title: Gaussian centers distinguish unitary, symplectic, and orthogonal families
accepted_units.why_material: Synthesizes the three transfers as common Gaussian variance with symmetry-dependent means and identifies zeros near the central point as the extra obstacle to recovering full Selberg-type analogues.
accepted_units.context_note: The distribution statements are conjectural comparisons; the fixed-deviation upper bound is GRH-conditional and the stronger analogue needs an additional zero-avoidance assumption.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mean and variance constants are display/OCR sensitive, but their signs, family ordering, and zero-proximity limitation are readable.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: One-sided zero control becomes a moment bound
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Under RH, a favorable-sign zero term permits a short-prime majorant for log|zeta|; high-moment concentration for two prime scales then controls upper tails strongly enough that layer-cake integration yields near-conjectural moments.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a one-sided, RH-conditional mechanism; it does not provide moment asymptotics or an unconditional replacement for zero control.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Prime-square mass predicts the family-dependent center
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The same prime-polynomial architecture transfers across families, while the negligible, positive, or negative prime-square term tracks the unitary, symplectic, or orthogonal shift in the expected Gaussian center.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The family arguments are sketches under GRH, exact constants are formula-sensitive, and the stronger Selberg analogues additionally require control of near-central zeros.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Tail estimates identify the moment-bearing value band
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A regime-matched upper-tail estimate not only bounds a moment integral but shows that values far below or above the natural logarithmic scale contribute negligibly to that moment.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The concentration statement uses the cited lower moment bound together with the paper's RH-conditional upper-tail theorem and does not assert a pointwise typical-value law.
